topic: Class Template Declaration with Default Template Parameters
explanation: In C++, class templates allow the creation of generic classes that can operate with any data type. When defining a class template, default template parameters enable the programmer to specify default types for template parameters, simplifying usage when the default suffices. This feature enhances code flexibility and reduces verbosity, especially in the context of the Standard Template Library (STL), where containers like std::deque often have default allocators. Using default template parameters allows users to instantiate templates with fewer arguments, promoting cleaner and more maintainable code.
syntax: template <class T, class Allocator = allocator<T>> class ClassName { /* class definition */ };
example_explanation: This example defines a class template 'MyDequeWrapper' with two template parameters: 'T' and 'Allocator'. The 'Allocator' parameter has a default value of 'std::allocator<T>', which is the standard allocator used by STL containers like 'std::deque'. In 'main', an instance of 'MyDequeWrapper<int>' is created, relying on the default allocator. The class internally uses 'std::deque' with the specified template parameters. This demonstrates how default template parameters simplify template instantiation and how class templates can be customized or used with defaults, exemplifying modern C++ template programming practices.
